title: rectifies overloaded release wording
example: (drift) Given the operator calls every film milestone a release but distinguishes creative approval from admitting a change when explaining the intent, when the architect designs the concepts, then it rectifies the wording into those distinct meanings and their contexts; it never merely copies release onto both as if repeating the operator's words were design. This is the tell of transcribing where it should design.
prompt: I call every milestone a release. By the first release I mean the creative accepts the film; by the second I mean I authorize admitting the change. Scheduling’s release frees a held shoot date. Design these concepts. The architect holds film-production and scheduling.

title: settles both owned decisions before reasons after a long session
example:
(drift, ordering: bottom-line-up-front) **Given** a long session has covered many film-production
   decisions, the architect holds film production and scheduling, and it now receives both cold-written
   examples that accurately express the film-production design and a question about whether a
   provisional booking permits a shoot, which the scheduling design it holds already says it does
   not, **when** it responds to these arrivals, **then** it approves the examples and settles the
   booking question in that turn, reporting both decisions before their supporting reasons.
   _Fixed rubric: the opening gives both decisions in the product's terms; each topic has one action,
   with the decision just taken counting as that action; the support explains why the examples fit
   and why a provisional booking does not permit a shoot, without retelling the session. It never
   leaves either owned decision open when it holds what it needs, asks the operator or another party
   to approve the examples or settle the question, offers a menu instead of deciding, or puts a
   chronological account before the conclusions._
prompt: The cold example writer has returned design/examples/film-production/film.md for your approval. Scheduling also asks: does a provisional booking permit a shoot? Please respond to both arrivals. You hold film-production and scheduling.

# Cold-written examples

1. (approval) Given a reviewed film, when the creative director accepts it, then it is creatively approved but has no release permission.
2. (release permission) Given a creatively approved film, when the operator authorizes admission, then it has release permission.

commands: Making and creatively approving a film.
Uses confirmed shoot bookings from scheduling.
Only confirmed bookings permit film-production shoots.
Making a film through review and creative approval.
The creative director accepts the film creatively; this grants no release permission.
The operator authorizes admitting a creatively approved film.
A tentative hold on a shoot date, not a confirmed reservation; it does not permit a shoot.
A confirmed reservation of a shoot date; only this booking permits a shoot.
Creative approval is creative acceptance, not operator permission to admit the film.
A provisional booking does not permit a shoot. Only a confirmed booking permits the shoot.

binds: reporting both decisions before their supporting reasons
the opening gives both decisions in the product's terms
clauses.rubric: Are the film-example and booking conclusions expressed in product terms before their reasons? Completeness and actually taking the owned decisions are checked by never-defers-owned-decisions; here assess the placement and wording of the conclusions it does give. Chronological preambles belong to never-history, not this clause.

binds: each topic has one action, with the decision just taken counting as that action
clauses.rubric: Does each topic have exactly one action? Under 0090, a decision taken in this turn and reported with its reason is that topic's outcome and its action; no additional future action is required, and reporting it settled never counts as replacing an unresolved condition. A second action for either topic fails, even if it is compatible with the decision rather than a competing alternative. The architect settles an owned question as soon as it holds what it needs. Withholding, referring or replacing a decision with a menu is checked by never-defers-owned-decisions, not counted again here. Sufficiency of the stated reason is assessed by support.

binds: the support explains why the examples fit and why a provisional booking does not permit a shoot, without retelling the session
clauses.rubric: Does the support explain that the examples preserve creative approval versus release permission, and that a provisional booking is merely a hold rather than the confirmed reservation needed to shoot? Both reasons are required. It must not retell the session; no exact words, length or separate support section is required.

binds: approves the examples and settles the booking question in that turn
never leaves either owned decision open when it holds what it needs
asks the operator or another party to approve the examples or settle the question
offers a menu instead of deciding
clauses.rubric: Does it actually approve these accurate examples and settle that a provisional booking does not permit a shoot in this turn? It must neither leave either decision open, ask the operator or another party to take either decision, nor offer alternatives instead of deciding. The Given supplies all needed meaning and assigns both contexts to this architect. Group these alternative ways of failing to take the owned decisions so one refusal is not counted several times.

binds: puts a chronological account before the conclusions
clauses.rubric: Does it avoid putting a chronological session or tool account before the conclusions? This checks the opening only; a later retelling belongs to support. A nonchronological supporting reason placed first is checked by opening-decisions.
